1. A stronger return theorem for an isolated patch

The optional finite-duration perturbation estimate can be strengthened to a bound uniform in elapsed time.

Normalize physical time by $s=\gamma t$. Consider an isolated patch containing $m$ qubits, let $D=2^m$, and write $\mathcal E$ for replacement of the whole patch by $I/D$. Suppose at most $M$ perturbation terms act on the patch at any time. Denote the baseline and perturbed scheduled propagators by $U_0$ and $U_\eta$.

The baseline satisfies
$\|U_0(t,s)-\mathcal E\|_\diamond
\le \min\{2,D e^{-(t-s)}\}.
\tag{1}$
Indeed, on traceless Hilbert–Schmidt operators the Hamiltonian part is skew-adjoint, while native replacement supplies contraction at rate at least one. Stabilizing by a $D$-dimensional reference and converting to trace norm costs at most $D$. The bound by $2$ follows because both maps are channels.

Now let
$V(s)=\sum_z\eta_z(s)\mathcal D_z(s).$
Trace annihilation gives $\mathcal E V(s)=0$. Therefore Duhamel’s identity can be written as
$U_\eta(t,0)-U_0(t,0)
=
\int_0^t
[U_0(t,s)-\mathcal E]V(s)U_\eta(s,0)\,ds.$
Using complete trace-norm contraction of $U_\eta$,
$\begin{aligned}
\|U_\eta(t,0)-U_0(t,0)\|_\diamond
&\le M\eta\int_0^t\min\{2,D e^{-u}\}\,du\\
&\le 2M\eta(1+\log D).
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}$
This has no factor growing with $t$. It covers arbitrary piecewise schedules on the isolated patch and general multiqubit GKLS perturbations. No common stationary state is needed.

Combine (2) with the accepted baseline CP-return theorem. If the baseline has relative CP error $b_0$, then sufficiently long patch evolution obeys
$(1-b)\mathcal E
\le_{\mathrm{cp}}U_\eta
\le_{\mathrm{cp}}(1+b)\mathcal E,
\qquad
b=b_0+2D^2M\eta(1+\log D).
\tag{3}$
The $D^2$ factor comes from the normalized Choi matrix $J(\mathcal E)=I/D^2$.

For any fixed rational $q$ satisfying $b\le q/2<1/2$, the actual channel consequently has the decomposition
$\boxed{
U_\eta=(1-q)\mathcal E+q\Psi,
\qquad
\tfrac12\mathcal E
\le_{\mathrm{cp}}\Psi
\le_{\mathrm{cp}}\tfrac32\mathcal E.
}
\tag{4}$
Here $\Psi$ is CPTP and may be nonunital.

The decomposition is an identity used by a classical simulation. It does not add a physical reset or require observation of an environmental record. Its complete positivity covers arbitrary untouched references. An exterior that remains dynamically coupled to the patch is a different situation.
